items.summary: A resting cortical spectrum carries a narrow peak near 10 Hz, a weaker and equally narrow peak near 20 Hz, and a broad 1/f background running beneath and above them. Mechanistic accounts locate each rhythm in a relaxation time, so a second band requires a second circuit, the ratio of the two amplitudes is predicted by nothing, and the broadband component is a residual. We compute all of it from one object. items.title: Cell death pathways in the pathogenesis of depression: mechanisms and therapeutic implications
items.summary: Depression is a highly prevalent and disabling psychiatric disorder with a complex and incompletely understood pathophysiology. Increasing evidence implicates regulated cell death (RCD), including apoptosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis, in neuronal vulnerability, synaptic impairment, and circuit dysfunction associated with depression. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current understanding of distinct cell death modalities in animal models of depression and human brain tissues, with particular emphasis on their molecular mechanisms and pathological consequences.
items.source: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology

items.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is entering higher education faster than universities can determine when it supports learning and when it substitutes for the intellectual work required to achieve it. This conceptual article examines this tension in Moroccan public universities through a systemic approach that connects learner cognition, pedagogical practices, institutional conditions, and national digital reform. items.summary: Emotion processing remains relatively intact throughout life, seemingly becoming more positive with age. Facial expressions reflect different emotions and involve distinct oscillatory responses, but whether aging affects these remains unclear. items.summary: Variations in neural circuitry, inherited or acquired, may underlie important individual differences in thought, feeling, and action patterns. items.summary: The significant heterogeneity of major depressive disorder (MDD) requires the development of interventions that directly target underlying cognitive or neurobiological mechanisms. items.title: Thalamic projections from the cerebellar nuclei receiving proprioceptive signals from the jaw muscles in rats
items.summary: The neural mechanisms involved in transmission of proprioceptive information from muscles are not fully understood. Proprioceptive signals from jaw-closing muscle spindles (jcms) are relayed to the supratrigeminal nucleus (Su5), and, then, from the Su5 to the thalamus including the oval paracentral nucleus (OPC) via the trigeminal lemniscal pathway and to the jcms-IntDL and jcms-MedDL (the dorsolateral hump of interposed cerebellar nucleus [IntDL] and the dorsolateral protuberance of medial cerebellar nucleus [MedDL], which were electrophysiologically identified to receive jcms-proprioception)

items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

OBJECTIVES: This meta-analytic review was conducted to determine the extent to which social relationships influence risk for mortality, which aspects of social relationships are most highly predictive, and which factors may moderate the risk. items.summary: Manual therapy commonly begins at the site where pain is reported.
